common.notReal: Not a real event: just for fun!

title.name: QUEST(ION)
title.subtitle: A SPACE MISSION DESIGN GAME
title.newConfirm: Start a NEW GAME? Your saved mission will be erased (your settings are kept).
title.p4note: 4 PLAYERS mode: each player picks a different role. (Visual for now: you play the same mission together.)

settings.title: SETTINGS
settings.note: Changes apply right away. You can open this menu from any screen.

mission.title: 📋 MY MISSION
mission.orbitOk: reaches Mars in {days} days · fuel {fuel}% (game value)
mission.logEmpty: Nothing yet. Your decisions will appear here.

pause.title: PAUSED
pause.note: The mini-game is paused. You can't go back in the middle of a mini-game, but you can quit it.

role.title: CHOOSE YOUR ASTRONAUT
role.sub: 1 PLAYER: pick one astronaut · 4 PLAYERS: each player picks a different role
role.mentor: Pick your astronaut. They will build and fly the mission with you. Tap "info" to learn what each role does.
role.mentor4: Each player picks a different role: P1, then P2, P3 and P4. Tap "info" to learn what each role does.

destination.title: CHOOSE YOUR DESTINATION
destination.sub: Click a planet to learn about it
destination.mentor: Let's start with Mars. Finish a mission there and the next planet unlocks. Click Mars to learn about it.
destination.locked: LOCKED · Complete the Mars mission to unlock
destination.lockedLong: Complete the Mars mission to unlock future destinations.

objective.question: WHAT IS THE GOAL OF YOUR MISSION?
objective.questionSub: Every mission starts with a science question. Only one objective is open for now: complete it to unlock the others.
objective.heading: OBJECTIVES
objective.inspired: Inspired by NASA's Mars Exploration Rovers: Spirit and Opportunity.
objective.chosen: Objective chosen! Press NEXT to continue

summary.title: MISSION SUMMARY
summary.sub: Check your choices before designing the spacecraft
summary.mentor: Great choice! This is your mission so far. Next, we will design a spacecraft that can reach Mars and do this science.

briefing.title: BUILD YOUR SPACESHIP
briefing.sub: Your mentor explains the workshop before you start
briefing.k1: 1. Build the cruise spacecraft that carries your rover to Mars: 5 stations, in order.
briefing.k2: 2. Watch your meters. Every part changes them.
briefing.budgetD: Each part has a price. Don't run out.
briefing.massD: Heavier ships need more fuel to launch.
briefing.earthD: Some parts help or harm Earth.
slides: Welcome to the workshop! Your rover rides inside an aeroshell; you build the cruise stage that flies it to Mars. Walk up to a station to pick its part.
Every part costs budget and adds mass. Real missions have a budget cap and a launch-mass limit, so pick wisely. (All meter numbers here are simulated game values.)
Your Earth responsibility meter only changes when an official NASA source backs the effect of a choice. Ready?

workshop.hintStart: Walk to station 1 and press [E] to choose a STRUCTURE.
workshop.hintNext: Walk to station {n} and press [E] to choose the {NAME}.
workshop.hintDone: Your spacecraft is assembled! Follow the pink path to the WAREHOUSE door ▶
workshop.assembledSub: Cruise stage ready to carry your rover to Mars. Next: pick the rover's science instruments.
workshop.reviewIntro: Let's review your build so far:
workshop.controls: Arrows / WASD: walk · E: use station · Q: ask the mentor

station.title: STATION {n}
station.noEarth: No official NASA source links this choice to an effect on Earth, so your responsibility level does not change.
station.mentorB: This is the setup the real MER spacecraft used. Compare it with options A and C before you install.
station.mentorC: This is real technology, but it was not MER's design. It could work better in some ways and worse in others.
station.mentorA: A simpler option. Think about what you gain and what you give up.
station.over: Over the budget cap! Choose a cheaper option.

warehouse.title: WAREHOUSE STORAGE
warehouse.mentor: Your rover base already drives, talks and has power. Inspect each table and pick the science instruments your mission needs!
warehouse.allDone: All 14 inspected! Walk to the EXIT ▶ to build your rover.
warehouse.controls: Arrows / WASD: walk · E: inspect table

card.title: INSTRUMENT CARD
card.wrong: ✕ Not quite. The right answer is highlighted. Try again!

assembly.title: BUILD YOUR ROVER
assembly.sub: Drag instruments from your kit onto the rover. The base rover already drives, talks and has power.
assembly.tip: Tip: add calibration targets so your measurements can be trusted.
assembly.simpl: Simplified: Mini-TES sits in the body and looks out through the mast.
assembly.mentor: Some tools only work on the arm. Not every great tool fits this rover!
assembly.undo: Z: undo last · drag & drop · ENTER: finish

assemblyResults.mentor: Modern tools are not "worse": they were just not built for a 2003 rover, and some answer a different question.

orbit.title: PLAN YOUR ORBIT
orbit.sub: Mentor tutorial: how to get from Earth to Mars
orbit.subFree: Aim the burn, set the power and pick the launch day
orbit.subWin: You reached Mars! Compare your attempts
orbit.drawHint: Before using the sliders, DRAW with the mouse the path you think the spacecraft will follow from EARTH to MARS's orbit. Then press NEXT.
orbit.controls: Drag sliders · Left/Right adjust · Tab next · SPACE launch · [?] help

launchReady.title: READY FOR LAUNCH
launchReady.sub: Your rover is packed inside the spacecraft, on top of the rocket.
launchReady.mentor: Okay, it's time! Next you will fly the rocket to orbit and protect it from falling space rocks.

meteor.title: LAUNCH!
meteor.sub: Protect your rocket on the way to orbit
steps: 1. Your rocket climbs on its own.
2. Move the blue SHIELD with the mouse (or WASD).
3. Push falling rocks away from the rocket.
4. 3 hits and the mission is lost.
5. Reach 200 km to get into orbit!
meteor.mentor: A meteor shower is crossing your launch path! Real rocks rarely hit rockets, but tiny space rocks and orbital debris are a real risk NASA tracks every day.
meteor.controls: Mouse / WASD: move shield · Esc: pause
meteor.hitMsg: A rock hit the rocket! Keep the shield between the rocks and the nose. {n} hits left.
meteor.reachedSub: Your rocket made it to 200 km
meteor.resultMentor: Nice flying! You lost {lost} hull point(s). Next: the long trip to Mars.
meteor.lostMentor: Don't worry: in the real world the team prepares for risks before launch. Try again!

rock.title: ROCK HUNTER
rock.sub: Meridiani Planum, Mars · Find 3 rocks with clues of ancient water
steps: 1. Drive the rover with A/D or the arrow keys.
2. Stop next to a rock and press SPACE to scan it with your instruments.
3. Read the clue and decide: COLLECT (E) or SKIP (Q).
4. Collect 3 promising samples before energy or time runs out.
5. Each scan uses energy. Choose wisely!
rock.mentor: Remember: a photo alone cannot prove there was water. Your instruments analyze each rock to find real clues.
rock.controls: A/D or Left/Right: drive · SPACE: scan · E: collect · Q: skip
rock.noInstrument: Your rover has no instrument that can read this clue well. (Pick the right instruments next time!)

comms.grab: Grab :: to drag an item up or down (or select with ↑↓ and move with W/S)

talk.title: TALKING TO EARTH
talk.sub: Your rover found clues! Now the data has to travel home.
talk.mentor: Science only counts once it reaches Earth. Let's get your data home!

signal.title: SIGNAL RUN
signal.badge: Simplified for fun: real links are planned by the team on Earth.
steps: 1. An orbiter flies across the Martian sky.
2. Move your antenna with A/D or the arrow keys.
3. Press SPACE to fire a data packet ONLY while the orbiter is inside the green LINK WINDOW.
4. Dust clouds block packets. Every shot costs energy.
5. Land 3 packets on the orbiter to send your data to Earth!
signal.mentor: Packets fired outside the window are lost in space, and that energy is gone. Wait for the right moment!
signal.controls: A/D or Left/Right: aim · SPACE: send packet (only in the LINK WINDOW)
signal.resultMentor: The team on Earth will see your clues about {min} minutes from now. That is how real Mars missions work!
signal.outMentor: The orbiter flew away. Another pass comes later: try again!

dashboard.title: MISSION COMPLETE!
dashboard.retryConfirm: Play the Mars mission again from the start? (Your settings and unlocks are kept.)
dashboard.end: Thanks for playing QUEST(ION)! Future destinations will open here.

detail.title: STAGE {n} · {NAME}
detail.sub: You vs the real mission: Spirit & Opportunity (MER)
detail.why: WHY THE REAL TEAM CHOSE THIS

4c.title: MISSION OBJECTIVE
4c.text: Destination locked: MARS! Now choose the science goal of your mission. Your objective decides the instruments and the spacecraft you will design next.

7b.title: BUILD YOUR SPACECRAFT
7b.text: Your mission is set: Mars, your crew and your objective. Now build the spacecraft that will carry your rover there, one station at a time.

9f.title: SCIENCE INSTRUMENTS
9f.text: Welcome to the warehouse! Your spacecraft is ready. Now choose the science instruments your rover will carry to hunt for clues of ancient water.

11a2.title: BUILD YOUR ROVER
11a2.text: Your instrument kit is ready. Now install each instrument in the right place on the rover before time runs out, and cover the 5 science requirements!

11e.title: PLAN YOUR ORBIT
11e.text: Your rover is equipped! Now plan the trip from Earth to Mars: choose the launch day, the burn power and the burn direction.

12.4.title: LAUNCH
12.4.text: Your orbit is planned and the launch window is open. Your spacecraft sits on top of the rocket: it's time to leave Earth!

13e-1.0.title: HOW THE REAL ROVERS STUDIED ROCKS
13e-1.0.text: Before you go hunting, see how Spirit and Opportunity really investigated rocks on Mars, step by step.

13e.title: ROCK HUNTER
13e.text: Your spacecraft reached Mars and the rover is on the ground at Meridiani Planum. Time to explore the rocks and look for clues of ancient water!

14f-1.0.title: WHAT THE REAL ROVERS SENT HOME
14f-1.0.text: Your hunt is over. Now discover what Spirit and Opportunity found on Mars and reported back to scientists on Earth.

15b.title: COMMUNICATIONS
15b.text: Your rover collected science on Mars. Now plan how to send it home: choose the route, the contact window and which data goes first.

16-0.title: TALKING TO EARTH
16-0.text: Your rover found clues on Mars. But science only counts once the data reaches Earth. Let's see how the real rovers sent it home.
